newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Algerian PM in Tunis for talks on trade row.
newsitem.headline: Algerian PM in Tunis for talks on trade row.

text.p: Algerian Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia arrives in Tunisia on Friday for a three-day visit amid a row over trade between the two countries, official sources said.

"Much progresses are needed in our partnership intiatives (joint companies). Regarding the volume of our trade exchanges, it is certainly behind our capacities and objectives...," Ouyahia told the Tunisian news agency TAP before arrival.
Tunisian Industry Minister Slaheddine Bouguerra told the parliament late on Thursday that there were "financial and trade difficulties" in the relations between the two countries.
Tunisian business sources have accused the Algerian authorities of limiting importation of Tunisian merchandise over the past few months without giving any reason.
They also say that Algeria is not buying goods from joint Algerian-Tunisian companies established to encourage trade between the two countries.

Tunisian officials said that because of trade problems with Algeria, exports to Algeria during the first eight months of 1996 fell to 73.9 million dinars ($73.9 million) from 95.8 million dinars during the same period in 1995.
Meanwhile, Tunisia's imports from Algeria, mainly oil, were up to 100.5 million dinars from 80.6 million dinars.

Algeria and Tunisia, are members along with Morocco, Mauritania and Libya of the Arab Maghreb Union (AMU), a regional grouping set up at a summit in 1989 to establish a common market between the five north African countries.
But so far, no concrete steps have been taken, mainly because of Algeria's five-year old civil strife, the pending Western Sahara issue, and Libya's disputes with the West. ($=one dinar)
